game: CHI@CIN Week 9 2025, kickoff 2025-11-02 13:00 ET, outdoors, CHI -3 / CIN +3, total 51.5

script.base: Market prices a close high-scoring game: CHI 27.2, CIN 24.2, not a blowout. CHI leads by about a field goal late. With D'Andre Swift (44 car/277 yds in weeks 6-8) and Roschon Johnson out, Kyle Monangai inherits the lead-back carries and CHI runs more once ahead. Both sides still throw because 51.5 and a 3-point spread keep CIN in it; Ja'Marr Chase (54 targets, 346 yds in those three weeks) stays the CIN hub if Joe Flacco plays.
script.flip1: CHI falls behind and abandons the run. Monangai's carry spike dies and Caleb Williams lives in the pass game (Rome Odunze/DJ Moore), while CIN's pass volume and Chase yards stay high or go higher.
script.flip2: Flacco's questionable shoulder shuts the CIN pass game down, or an uncharted outdoor slog cuts the 51.5. CIN leans Chase Brown/Samaje Perine on the ground, Chase and Tee Higgins unders hit, and the favorite clock-kill still feeds Monangai.

injury_fallout: Pre-game nflverse report, not inactives: CHI RB Swift Out (groin) and RB Roschon Johnson Out (back) vacate the backfield; only Monangai (25 car/124, 4 tgt/38 in weeks 6-8) has a real RB sample, so he gains carries and the Swift checkdowns (Swift 6 tgt/107). WR Luther Burden III Out (concussion; 7 tgt/72) pushes targets toward Odunze (21), Moore (17), Olamide Zaccheaus (16) and Colston Loveland (12), not a clear Cole Kmet bump (Kmet line 22.5, last4 10/46/0/16). CHI DE Dominique Robinson Out (ankle) and LB Amen Ogbongbemiga Questionable (knee) thin CHI's front. CIN DE Trey Hendrickson Doubtful (hip) lowers pressure on Williams; LB Logan Wilson Doubtful (calf) and LB Oren Burks Questionable (groin) help CHI TE/RB/slot; CB Marco Wilson Doubtful (hamstring) thins the CIN secondary for Odunze/Moore. CIN G Dalton Risner Questionable (illness) is an OL flag for Brown. Flacco Questionable (shoulder) is the pass-game kill switch for Chase/Higgins/Noah Fant. Sources: pack injury report and weeks 6-8 usage; final inactives not in pack.

matchup.shell: MOFO/MOFC and man/zone rates are not in the pack (no coverage charting). Proxies: CIN blitzes only 21% so most snaps are a four-man look; CHI blitzes 31%. CIN YPA allowed is high to every field (left 7.81 on 113, middle 7.49 on 57, right 8.05 on 99).
matchup.pressure: CIN pressure threat is down with Hendrickson Doubtful and a 21% blitz. CHI EPA/db is +0.17 vs blitz and +0.07 vs no blitz, so Williams is fine either way and deep air (Odunze 326 air yards on 21 targets in three weeks) is less likely to be killed by pressure. CHI blitzes 31%; CIN EPA/db is +0.03 vs blitz but -0.12 when not blitzed, so most CHI snaps are the look where CIN has been worse.
matchup.bleeds: CIN run defense allows 5.17 YPC and 28 runs of 10+ (8 games) plus 30 passes of 20+ for 280 yards. CHI run defense allows 5.31 YPC and 28 runs of 10+ (7 games); pass bleed is the middle (9.56 YPA on 45) more than left 7.62 or right 7.04, with 21 passes of 20+ for 207.
matchup.overlap: Core overlap is Chase, the 18-target/game primary, into CHI's middle-field bleed and a lighter pass rush (Robinson out), in a 51.5 game. Second overlap is Monangai's expanded carry share into a 5.17 YPC CIN run defense in a CHI-lead script. Odunze's air-yard profile fits CIN's explosive-pass leak, but the yards have not followed (177 on 326 air).

Monangai last4 rush yds 18, 19, 81, 24 (only 2 of 4 clear 19.5) on a complement role of 8.3 car/g and 4.96 YPC beside Swift's 6.3 YPC. Chase last4 rec yds 110, 94, 161, 91 vs 92.5 (3 of 4 over) on 115 ypg and 18 targets in weeks 6-8. Higgins last4 22, 62, 96, 44 vs 38.5; Fant 26, 27, 44, 41 vs 27.5; Brown rush last4 27, 42, 108, 73 vs 42.5 but splitting with Perine (22 car/141 in three weeks). Odunze last4 69, 32, 31, 114 vs 62.5, two duds. Moore last4 38, 42, 43, 73 vs 43.5. No similar-defense charting beyond the season defensive splits in the pack.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and both legs lost. Flacco was limited or inactive, CIN's offense stayed in the no-blitz looks where their EPA/db is -0.12, and Chase was the player CHI took away, finishing under 92.5 the way the 91-yard game already showed he can. Separately, CHI trailed early, Williams threw to Odunze and Moore, and an unlisted back or a pass-only script held Monangai near the 18-19 yard complement games instead of Swift's 90-yard rushing pace. A late inactive or a snap limit we do not have yet would have made the 19.5 line correct rather than stale. That counter is stronger on Chase than on Monangai, which is why Chase stays a lean and Monangai stays the only strong leg.
slip_story: One competitive high-total story, not a mix of under and overs: CHI -3 controls the late clock so Monangai rush yards over 19.5, and CIN stays close enough at a 51.5 total that Chase receiving yards over 92.5 still cashes if Flacco plays. Do not add a total under, a Chase Brown rush over (needs CIN to run while trailing less), or a second Monangai market. No TD legs. Max two players.
